value.definition: ordering_depth(R) is the longest-chain cardinality of the required precedence relation R: the number of items in the longest chain of R, counted in items rather than edges
value.generator_form: for N items at depth d, expose exactly one chain containing d items as its d - 1 cover relations, and leave the remaining N - d items explicitly unconstrained; randomise chain membership, chain order and presentation order from separate domain-separated streams of the recorded seed
value.grid_rule: not decided at Stage 2. Section 6.2's ordered grid of at most five admissible settings is the Stage 5 boundary-calibration output recorded in parameters.p1.admissible_set (register item D6); anticipating it here would pre-empt the calibration that selects it

rejected_alternatives.n_items: item count is not a property of the ordering relation at all, so it would make the focal parameter a second copy of the target parameter n_items and confound the two constraints the pair is designed to separate
rejected_alternatives.edge_count: counts stated requirements rather than the depth of the order; under the canonical generator it is d - 1 and so carries the same information, but off it a wide shallow relation and a deep narrow one can share an edge count
rejected_alternatives.linear_extension_count: measures constrainedness, which is a defensible different construct; it is not a depth, is #P-hard in general, and is not monotone in any quantity the prompt states

records.frozen_by: the investigator, in the Stage 2 decision instruction of 2026-08-11
records.evidence: Amendment A4, accepted verbatim: 'Freeze: ordering_depth(R) = longest-chain cardinality' and 'Also freeze the generator so the statistic uniquely determines the intended manipulation'. Both halves are implemented in dci.v19.ordering. The generator produces exactly one chain of d items with the remaining N - d explicitly unconstrained, exposes the chain's d - 1 cover relations rather than its closure, requires 2 <= d <= N, and randomises chain membership, chain order and presentation order from separate domain-separated streams of the recorded seed. Under that form edge count, constrained-item count and free-item count are functions of d alone, which a test asserts at every admissible depth; off the canonical form a single depth admits relations differing in all three. Larger d is recorded as the nominal harder direction. The retained depths are NOT decided here: section 6.2's ordered grid is the Stage 5 calibration output parameters.p1.admissible_set (register item D6), and the domain refuses a Stage 2 value that carries one.

records.evidence: Amendment A2, accepted verbatim: 'Adopt the corrected verifier semantics.' The disposition is 'corrected', not 'reused_unchanged': section 14.2 permits reuse only after a hash and semantic audit, the audit demonstrated three defects, and section 10.6 requires repair and re-audit before freeze. records.frozen_by: the investigator, in the Stage 2 decision instruction of 2026-08-11
records.evidence: Amendment A3, accepted verbatim: 'Adopt exact two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson intervals.' Recovery established that the inherited gate used the Wilson score interval, which is not exact, and that only Wilson reproduces the 73-per-truth-class and 876-label counts section 10.4 preserves; both halves of that sentence could not hold. The exact interval reaches the 5% ceiling at n = 72, so the Tier-1 planning total becomes 864 labels. Register row D45 is added, because section 10.4 cites D9, which is the construction bootstrap and does not cover this decision. dci.v19.reliability.recover_inherited_interval retains the arithmetic so a reviewer can re-check the choice.

value.remediation: a unit that fails is repaired and re-audited under a fresh prospectively specified audit, not by extending the original sample. Section 10.6: 'A demonstrated semantic or verifier defect requires repair and re-audit before freeze; collecting more confirmatory data is not a remedy for invalid measurement.' Extending a sample after seeing an error makes the realised size a function of the observed data, so the nominal 95% coverage no longer describes the procedure that was run
value.citation: section 10.4 + Stage 2 amendment A3, register row D45

records.frozen_by: the investigator, in the Stage 2 decision instruction of 2026-08-11
records.evidence: Amendment A3's design half, accepted verbatim: 'Use the strict fixed design: n = 72 per truth class; zero observed errors are required to pass; any observed error fails the audit; after failure, repair/re-audit the verifier using a fresh prospectively specified audit. Do not conditionally extend the original sample to 110.' The design is a separate artifact from the interval because the interval alone does not determine a decision rule: one error in 72 gives an exact upper bound of 0.0750 and fails, while the same error in 110 gives 0.0496 and would pass. 110 is the SMALLEST sample at which one error clears the 5% ceiling, which is why it is the extension named and forbidden. tier1_certificate_under refuses a realised audit the design does not admit before the bound is allowed to speak, and reports which rule was broken.

clauses.uncovered_semantics: the abstraction places each declared item at an integer position and checks the closure over those positions; it does not establish that a reader would identify the item at that position AS that item, which is the identification the list policy's label rule decides

the abstraction equates distinctness with the token counts agreeing under the frozen tokenisation. Invisible characters no longer defeat it - they are removed before tokenising - but confusables remain outside any automated rule: a Cyrillic look-alike is a different string and NFKC does not merge it, so a projection satisfying this clause can still look to a reader like a repeated word. Section 10.6 assigns homoglyphs to human audit material, not to code

the abstraction counts sentences as the frozen segmentation does, and that segmentation strips the list grammar's own markers and treats each remaining line as a sentence, so a projection satisfying this clause need not contain that many sentences as a reader would count them. The coupling is now explicit - the marker patterns are inside this clause's hash - but it is not removed

records.frozen_by: the investigator, in the Tier-1 audit protocol decision of 2026-08-11
records.evidence: Section 10.4 requires 'human-adjudicated' true-failure and true-pass examples and never states the human procedure. Section 8.6's two-independent-reviewers-plus-third-adjudicator rule governs semantic review of compositions; extending it to the Tier-1 reliability audit is this decision, made explicitly rather than by inference. The accepted protocol: 100 human-authored candidates per verifier unit per INTENDED truth class (1,200 total), authored and hash-bound in the frozen audit split before review begins; one frozen three-person panel, reviewers A and B judging every candidate independently and without communicating, reviewer C adjudicating only A/B disagreements; reviewers blinded to intended truth class, verifier verdict, arm, target/focal role and internal constraint or verifier identity; human adjudication alone establishes whether the natural-language requirement is satisfied, never the verifier implementation; NO cross-crediting - a candidate adjudicated into the other class is discarded, not moved; a case whose disagreement adjudication does not resolve is marked unusable and excluded; after adjudication the first 72 retained cases per unit per class are taken in the manifest order frozen before any review, and remaining usable reserve is ignored; no adaptive top-up and no conditional extension, with a stratum below 72 returning AUDIT_POOL_INSUFFICIENT rather than prompting further authoring; and a case may serve only one verifier unit. 100 rather than 72 because a case's truth class is established by the reviewers: authoring exactly 72 reaches 72 adjudicated cases with probability about 0.55 even when mis-adjudicated cases are credited to the other class, and essentially never under the no-cross-crediting rule this protocol adopts. 72 remains the denominator entering the exact two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson interval, with zero verifier errors permitted, so amendment A3's design check sees exactly the sample it fixes. The selection order is a function of case content fixed by the manifest hash before any reviewer saw anything, so it cannot respond to verifier output.
